comment: Tons of friendly people with their dogs, great trail, part of the trail was closed for a few days for invasive species management. North side has a lot of hills and meadows, south side is mostly tree covering

The south part route is wide and easy. Then east to north is open view grassland. Make sure wear hat. 

Then the west to south route is hilly and narrow. This side Not popular probably. Make sure bug spray
Lots of dog poop
Great trail, well maintained. No real views, but nice tree cover for most of the trail, great for summer. No bikers.

Awesome trail!  Very nice tree covering and path is in great shape.  Went all the way to McGowan entrance, was 4.0 miles round trip. Excellent jogging trail, some nice rolling hills.  Only down side is free range dogs.
Mix of Icy and wet/drying out trails

Great nature walk through the forest where you can take your well behaved dog off leash.  There aren’t many places in the GTA where you can hike with your dog completely off leash.   Worth the drive from Mississauga!!
Walking conditions even in the snow were excellent bc this trail is very well travelled! Lots of people. Lots of dogs. Very lovely!

Very popular dog walking area since it’s off leash. You’ll run into a lot of people but most are quite friendly. Trails are wide and snow covered from recent storm. Some slippery downhill areas where crampons would be ideal. We didn’t follow the entire posted route. Have your GPS handy as there are multiple trails to take.
I heard gunshots
My wife and just loved this place. It's beautiful, easy for hiking.
Easy trail, some elevation.  Nothing technical but some fitness needed
Easy and lots of doggos
Great trail for running! Not too busy but you will make some furry friends along the way.

Great trail, lots of wide walking areas. Not very busy, but ran into a few folks along the way. Dog park at McCowan entrance had chairs for the humans to sit and socialize and that looked lovely! No bugs.
No bathrooms; so come prepared in that way :)

Amazing off leash dog trail. Very dry in most parts, some areas with mud/water. But there are walkways to keep you dry. There is a shooting range near by, so use caution if your dog does not like noises like fireworks or thunder. Parking is free: first come first serve but a decent number of spots available off Kennedy Rd.
lots of parking at kennedy rd, trail was big and cleared out but there are very few directions/signs so would be hard to navigate without a map or phone.
.gg
Some wet areas that require walking on logs. Lots of dogs
Great hike
Muddy, wet
Icy
So crowded. Dogs off leash

A very well maintained trail with a variety of conditions (multi use trail, gravel, etc.) Enjoyed the variety of views (forest, ravine, and farmlands) and particularly enjoyed the number of amazing dogs on the trail. Beware if you are not a fan of dogs as this regional forest is an off-leash dog park as well. There are two parking areas on either the dead-end of Kennedy and Davis and off McCowan.

Great off-leash forest walk. Friendly dog owners and well-behaved dogs! 

Good options to walk different loops or go for the longer walk and take in both the Kennedy Rd trailhead over to Warden Rd dog park. Wide trails on soft forest bed with slight elevation. Generally an easy and enjoyable trail.  

Mix of hardwood and evergreen trees make for an enjoyable afternoon trail walk.
Met Scarlett’s nephew Remi on the trail!
Great trails!   Love this YRF tract. Always so many walkers hikers and dogs!!  Fall colours showing everywhere.
The north edge goes into the ravine so hilly and more rustic than the other parts.
Moderate and wasn’t much to see.. but was a great hike.
Well maintained trail,  very light traffic, beautiful landscape.
Nice range of landscapes, some mucky bits for muck-loving pups!
Great trail but watch out for the water. My dog loves it and got covered in mud.
brng comfortable shoes, water, snack and walking stick for steep up and downhills
Really nice trail - there's plenty of shade. Good workout route as well.
Lots of poison ivy
mix of single track and wide flat trail w LOTS of hills

Excellent trail with wide walking paths. The side trails allow you to make the trail shorter.lota of dogs on the trail, since dogs are allowed off leash. Clean and largely amongst the trees except from the section that goes to McCowan road parking lot. New plantation in this region. You can choose to bypass that section using a side trail.
Good walking and riding trails. A busy spot but lots of trails
Too many bugs. I couldn’t finish the trail. Also mainly in the sun.

Great trail! Easy to walk through. Certain places were muddy but they were easy to pass through. Quite a bit of mosquitoes so a bug spray is recommended! Dogs are allowed off leash with certain rules in place so it’s a bonus! Enjoy the fresh air!

People just park on the road by the trail entrance. It’s at a dead end. There were a lot of people and dogs at the start but it wasn’t busy on the trails. There are many trail options to take once inside. The dogs loved it! When the trail passed by the stream or two ponds they ran right into them and got so muddy, so be prepared. It rained yesterday so some parts of the trail were also muddy. The trail out to McCowen parking lot did not have tree cover so it was not great for sun coverage. Mosquitos weren’t too bad when moving. An amazing off leash area!
good
Trails in good condition except for 4 or 5 muddy spots.. no bugs yet (5/16).
Super easy hike! Very quiet and peaceful with minimal muddy spots/puddles to walk over on logs. Absolutely a park that you want to bring your dog to as the dogs and people are kind.
A couple of big puddles where you have to tip toe over logs. All else very dry.
Overall conditions are better. Some parts very muddy but could avoid with minor detours
We enjoyed the trail.  So many dogs (thats a good thing). Lots of trees.  Plenty of options to make the trail longer or shorter.  Lots of parking as well
Muddy in spots.  Lots of dogs off leash but all super friendly. Lots of off shoot trails
What a great place to let our dogs play, run, explore off leash. The trails are easy to walk. People we met are super friendly & engaging.
Some slopes and muddy sections, but all in all, a nice hiking trail.
Best hike in the area. Nice valleys
Icy & muddy… but pretty!
Quite muddy in spots. A fairly easy trail otherwise.

Simple trail with some variety and optional side trails - mostly flat, nothing challenging. 
Dogs can be off leash and there were plenty there - mostly well behaved.
Always a great trail! Found a couple ticks on the dog the weekend of Oct 14, just a heads up for anyone heading out before snowfall.

A perfect day for a hike. Trail was not busy. It was in perfect condition except for the horse poop which is always a problem. I wish the York Region forest would make horse owners bag their horses in the park.
Very nice trail, lots of people, no bugs for me!
Beautiful trails today, no bugs!

Nice trail
You can walk easily

Nice and easy. No bugs today!
Off leash friendly
Amazing hike. Just wish some of the low lying areas had a bridge as they can be impassable when there is any rain
A bit muddy in lower areas after the rain, but as always nice
One of the best trails in York Region for dog owners and their dogs.
Little to no bugs this morning but temp has dropped off to 21c
Off leash dog trail, so great for the pup

Easy, flat trail. Not a trail to get a good hiking workout in, but great for a stroll. Minimal incline. Mix of tree coverage. Lots of dogs and signs saying they allow off leash. Walk past a dog park, so can stop in there if ya fancy.

Overall, I had a great time on the hike despite encountering some mud patches along the way. It's a very foresty vibe, which adds to the charm. It's important to have the app open to stay on track and not miss any turns.
Beautiful trail - tricky at times to know where to turn but app helps. Now a leash free trail so many large dogs loose on the trail.
Only two little patches of mud to deal with on the main forest path.
A bit muddy in places
Still muddy but great trail!
Excellent trail.  Nice hard pack snow.  Enjoyed the elevation changes.   Plenty of trees and fresh air.
Very icy
Dog friendly, off lease trail.
This is an off leash park :)
its off leash park
Gorgeous winter trail
Off leash dog trail. No snow today but lots of leaves on ground and dry/frozen ground. Not slippery but worth keeping your wits about you on the downhill stretches.
This is an excellent trail through a lovey part of York Regional Forest!! Very dog friendly.. lots of great scenery and moderately challenging! Definitely on my list of trials to walk again!

I did the 7k route in November 2022 and it was a great hike with lots of elevation changes for a good workout and a beautiful coniferous forest. The trail on the northern part of the map, going west to east, is a single tract and I initially missed it as I was expecting a wider trail. But I received an alert I was off the trail so quickly righted my mistake! Be careful on the sketchy bridge over the little stream! This in an off- leash trail so do expect to see dogs running towards you - I went on a Tuesday, around 2pm and still saw about a dozen dogs. It also has a fenced in dog play area.

- multiple trails
- family friendly, I saw kids and seniors exploring the trail
- dog friendly
Fell through an old bridge across a bog. Beware
Mostly wide open trails. I would rate as easy, not moderate.
Good conditions, great for off leash dog walking.

Love that dogs can be off leash on this trail! I like that there are a lot of alternative routes and options once you’re in the forest. If your dog isn’t used to horses, be aware that riders also use this trail. There’s also a couple creek areas - my pup got pretty muddy. There are parts of the trail as outlined in the app that aren’t shaded. But you can also just stay inside the forest if it’s hot.
Good trail for running! Minor hills but enough to get the heart pumping!
Beautiful as always! Extra signage added so you can navigate easier!

Was a great way to spend my Sunday, not super challenging and is off leash for dogs. Only thing is when you get to McGowan by the dog park the trail marker is a little hard to spot. its in the parking lot corner, dont need to go on the road.
The majority of the trail is pretty easy but it gets tough towards the end. There are many trees blocking the way and doesn’t seem like an actual trail. But we enjoyed it overall.
Pleasant trail, mix of open and forest. No mosquitos. The most poison ivy I've ever seen, but the trail is usually wide enough to avoid it.
Beautiful trail
The trail was good and shaded, some  bugs in the forest but overall was wide, and easy to walk in. Near the tree planting area had lots of bugs, but did not bite just a bit annoying.

Beautiful forest with lots of variety in trees and birds. Only downside is noise pollution from what sounds like a gun club or someone target shooting on their nearby property - kind fo ruins your ability to immerse yourself in the forest.
Great. Forested in southern part. Muddy at points, logs laid to cross, don’t wear dress shoes, mosquitoes so wear long sleeves, fallen trees can be bypassed creatively.
it was a great hike
Always a great trail, muddy in some parts so I recommend good hiking shoes

Moderate trail, quite muddy in spots through the forest. Dogs are allowed to be offleash in this area but we didn't encounter that many. (maybe busier on the weekend). I discovered the dog park at the McCowan Road entrance so my dogs enjoyed some offleash time before we headed back to the forest. Overall, a nice hike.
Natural, well maintained.  Way finding along trails needed.

Soon to formally be a trail for walking dogs off leash. Well overdue for a great number of dog lovers and nature lovers. Some parts are full sun and open, other parts are under canopy of forest. Overall a lovely walk. All dogs were friendly and well behaved.￼￼ Personally I think we need more of these.￼
Too many unleashed dogs made this trail not too enjoyable for hikers
Love this trail!

great trail with lots of old forest and some new forest. there's a delightful amount of hills. only issue is people letting their aggressive dogs run around off leash. I had one bite my hand after the owner leashed it and told me to walk by, but it lunged at me while the owner was trying to stop it.

Gorgeous trail that takes you through a variety of landscapes, from old forests to young forests to fields. Can be wet, slushy, slick, and a little muddy in parts at this time of year, as the snow melts. Just plan accordingly with footwear. Took about 2 hours to complete the full trail. Would definitely recommend and will definitely be back in the summer.
Young and old forest nicely combined makes it a unique experience
Warm weather meant lots of puddles and slosh. Bring proper footwear and you'll have a great time!

Nice trail, however, we encountered lots of dogs off leash and owners who didn’t feel the need to manage or even watch their dogs.  If you aren’t comfortable with strange dogs approaching you I would avoid this trail.
Great skiiing

Great workout today…snow not too flat so careful on the ankles. 
Weather temp was perfect not to cold and no wind. Great day
Nice winter trail. A lot of dogs here
Nice New Year walk today

Great little easy hike with fun trails, good for dogs as well.

I usually see deer here. One of my favourite tracts, absolutely beautiful. Plenty of new trees planted, be sure to respect the signs that ask you not to go off trail as that could damage newly planted trees & vegetation.
Great walk with the dog.  Several routes to take to make your walk longer or shorter.

There is a gorgeous natural overgrown area with tree stumps hidden at the northwest corner of the trail that is hard to find the way in/out of but apparently part of the trail. Would love to go back and figure out the trails.

Beautiful and lots of option to build your own route. You can start near the dog park (Mccowan) or near the forest entrance (Kennedy Rd). The former is easier on younger kids but it’s not shaded. Forest trail has no signage once you get started so it’s easy to get lost! Overall, a lovely place to spend your day.
Fantastic.
A quick hike before the rain comes in the afternoon.  Very nice cool weather
Nice trail but won't come back because the constant gun fires.
Trails are not maintained, muddy, no signs. Easy to get lost
Could use some signage to help navigate the paths and property as a whole.

Besides the constant gun fire going off it was great. I went during the week at 930. Took my dog. I saw one women on my hike. Lots of wooded area. I did get lost once because I lost reception on my phone and went off the trail.
Lots of variety in terms of shade, sun and elevation.
Enjoyable moderate 1.5hr walk through meadows and forest.

Close to a gun range so there are constant gunshots in the background.

Really enjoyed the challenge of the trails, good practice!

Positives: saw and heard lots of birds, squirrels and wildlife, very shaded and not very buggy and the main trail is wide and the parking is decent (it’s no exit)
Negatives: lots of tree branches on side paths and horse manure was around on the paths. Found out there’s a stable right beside the trail by accidentally almost walking onto their property.
Overall I would go back!

Do you like hearing gunshots from a shooting range and constantly jumping around large piles of horse dung? This is the trail for you!

In all honestly, I still gave it 3 stars. It's still a real hike in the real woods, with about 1/3 out in a meadow in the sun (bring the sunblock and water). But there's nothing extremely interesting or sight reward, other than some interesting birds to watch.
amazing definitely going back
You need to walk under the sun most of the trail. There were off leash dogs that I didn’t like. Overall not the beat trail!
No trail markers but paths were easy enough to follow.
Super Nice !! Technical enough!! No caterpillars as off June 6 !!
the trail was scenic

Hope they change this to easy. Lots of people, dogs and toddlers enjoying the trail. I agree it's unsightly to see those cut trees everywhere. I think it's a better experience if the trail's reversed: 2/3 is like a walk in the part. Only gets slightly less easy on the way back.

Combined the East and West trail (towards the dog park) to make a nice 8.6km trail run. Really nice trail except for the dog owners not picking up after their dogs. But overall enjoyable, easy to navigate, good variety of wide and narrow trails.
Good variety and wide track good for group snowshoeing or trail runs
this is a must see. it's beautiful.
Nice trail.  Will definitely come back.

Light traffic at the beginning. Busy around the off leash dog area. Some parts were muddy but easy to walk around. There is no proper signal around the off leash dog area to connect reconnect the trail (way back). Beautiful sights of pine trees. Lots of birds.

Decent trail. My reason for the three stars though is there’s been fresh logging so lots of stuff cut down, which really detracts from the natural beauty of the forest. It’s to be expected since it is a tract managed by York Region. If you’re looking for undisturbed nature there are better trails.
Beautiful as always, lots of trees cut down and branches and cutoffs along trail
Beautiful trail! Not too busy. Didn’t have enough time to try the side trail, but we’ll be back!
Super quiet hike, all you hear is the rustling of the trees and birds chirping.
Great for both hiking and mountain biking

It was lightly trafficking and a lot of parking space. The trails were too mudy after yesterday's rain. Some passages were impossible to pass. The inside the trail is poorly maintained as I could hardly find my way out. Lots of broken trees on the way.

Trail was full of dog poop both bagged and loose - owners PLEASE pick up after your dogs!! 

Did the 7km walk in 1.5h. It was easy and shouldn’t be rated moderate. As of April 2, all of the ice had melted but it wasn’t really muddy. There’s a parking lot at the dog park, and on the other end of the trail (Kennedy and Davis) people just park on the side of the road. Was not very busy for a long weekend and there was plenty of room to socially distance. Overall a nice little walk just outside of Toronto.
Beautiful and a great exercise! So many cut trees at the entrance was a disturbing scene though.
Nice trail with varying scenary. Some sections still very icy in late March and crampons are recommended.

Pretty. Mix of open and wooded.

This is a really nice trail that is wide and clearly visible. There is very good size parking lot. There is garbage cans. There’s a nice dog off leash park by the parking lot. Great trail!

Nice trail,
Last section is not easy for biking, Better with hiking.

Wonderful trail through different types of forest, as well as a pretty open area on the east side with small new-growth evergreens. Even on an overcast day past the peak of the fall colours, it was still beautiful and very enjoyable. So many leaves on the ground that it was occasionally hard to see the smaller paths, but the map on the app helped us stay on track. Highly recommend this trail for a peaceful day out!
End of Kennedy. Easy
Beautiful hike, lots of fall colours, and plenty of simple hills! No bugs but lots of friendly dogs.
Nice trail. Great for all levels. There needs to be better trail markers, though. I don’t know if there are any, actually.
Beautiful
Went with my puppy to get some leash training time in. It was a nice trail, not busy midday. Will return without the pup to do the full trail.
Beautiful forest. Lots of rolling hills and scenic meadows
easy trail but nice

Fantastic area to hike. Lots of side trails. Routes for all fitness levels. We can't wait to go back!
Other than a lot of off-leash dogs..., Fantastic!
Forest was great, conservation area had a bit more traffic but again it is a Saturday morning on a nice day. Great for dogs.
decent trail not allot of ppl
a little creepy at parts, but generally a very cool trail!
Awesome if you have dogs but also 5 stars for hiking.  Lots of incline hikes which give you enough challenges and different types of landscapes.
hardly any mosquitos or people! Really peaceful hike but a good workout!
Mixed terrain- forested and open fields. Not buggy. Few people. Easy- moderate. Great day!
beautiful! lots of different scenic views! 10/10 recommend
Good trail. Kids love it. Not well marked out.

The trail is quite interesting! With ups and downs; a shaded forest and open fields. There’s even a dried out stream. There are actually two loops. The trail signages are NOT well marked. However, follow the red path on the app’s map which appears to be very accurate. The lower loop is through the shaded forest, fully shaded. Very pleasant! Beware of the mosquito population though! The upper loop, which is near McCowan Road is running along open fields. Totally different experience. I liked both, but it’s a bit harsh to be under the scorching Sun in the open fields. There are some educational stations, a dog unleash area, a parking lot near the upper loop. The trail condition is great. I met only a few people during my 2-3 hours on the trail, on a Saturday.
awesome hike with convenient parking. the reforestation trail was a nice touch

Beautiful trail, but I present to you a side trail not on the map which extends the trip to a beautiful 5.4km deep woods walk. I call it Smugglers Run! My gift to you, reader, see my recording for a map.

I would consider this neither easy nor a moderate trail! Something in between! In this trail, you would see both narrow and wide walkway. Some parts are shady and other parts open trail! Traffic is low although not too far from cities! You would cross a dog park somewhere in the middle of your route (where it touch the road), anywhere else you have to keep your pet on leash! Trail’s downside: lots of mosquitoes in woody part of it.
Beautiful trail. Wide and mostly flat.
Great trial! Mixed with easy and challenging parts, from flat area to high hills, a beautiful valley, and both shaded and open areas.

Great place to hike. We’ve only been twice. So many off shoot trails. Some wet spots some muddy areas. We went in mid May. 
If any thing I would like to see all the secondary trails marked.
Very nice trail. I would give 5 stars if it had signs on the way. There are so many different trails and we had to look on the map on the phone a lot to stay on the right trail.
A few nice spots (including a large reforestation area, and a twisty forest). There are better hiking options in the area, though.
great hike - lots of trail options to mix it up !

A huge chunk of the trail was easy and flat so not really moderate until the super narrow path. The loop connects 2 parking areas (one at Kennedy and the other official one at McCowan). Lots of fallen and dead trees which make it more fun and challenging to climb under or over. Very well kept and didn't see any garbage around. Nice to have trails open at this time. Not too many people and easy to keep a distance from others.
Good conditions.  Dry in the Savannah area.  Dry in the forest trail except 2 big puddles that require tip-toeing across logs.
great trail. challenging without being too difficult to walk. some icy sections but otherwise well maintained
Nice trail, to many dogs off leash, dog owners need to pick up after their pets, beginning of trails littered with waste.

beautiful Trail. We decided to do some off-trail hiking at our own Peril, and ended up in a bit of a swampy area. But it was a beautiful mini adventure. Ended up in some nice meadows and pine trees. beautiful fall day for a hike.
Stevie had a great time. Followed the trail on the map, good hike.

Bring a hat and bug spray for the flies and mosquitoes in the summer. A nice easy trail with the odd challenge. There is one short part that is over grown and not easy to distinguish the path from just brush. Mostly shade but with a large section of open/easy terrain.
Great hike, lots of trail options and you can go for hours. Wear bug spray and you will be ok. Excellent trail running in the shade. Not too busy as well.

very buggy, lots of downed trees had to walk the bikes quite a bit, where the creek runs through the trails, each location was very muddy and the bridges are no longer bridges I.e. the bridge in the picture for the trail has fallen apart.
